correctness.rationale: Direct differentiation gives \(\dot P=c y^2+(d-a)x^2+d x(\sinh x-x)\) for \(P=xz-y^2/2+cxy+b^2x^2/2\). On \(a\le d\) all terms are nonnegative. Boundedness makes \(P\) bounded, so their time integrals are finite; uniform-continuity/Barbalat arguments force \(x,y,z\to0\). A bounded complete orbit has \(P\to0\) at both time ends, hence constant \(P\) and is the origin. Integrating the same coboundary against any compactly supported invariant probability measure forces support on the common zero set, again only the origin. For \(a>d\), strict monotonicity of \(\sinh x/x\) on \(x>0\) gives exactly one positive nonzero equilibrium and its negative. The symbolic differentiation was independently replayed.
residual_risks: The theorem concerns bounded/compact recurrent dynamics; it does not classify unbounded trajectories when \(a\le d\) or non-equilibrium compact dynamics when \(a>d\).

value.rationale: This converts a local pitchfork threshold into an exact global compact-recurrence boundary for a nonlinear jerk family and classifies every compact invariant probability measure on the closed side. The monotone coboundary is a reusable structural obstruction, not a numerical attractor check.
residual_risks: The result is confined to the symmetric hyperbolic-sine model with positive b,c,d.

final_claim: For the symmetric hyperbolic-sine jerk flow \(\dot x=y,\ \dot y=z,\ \dot z=-ax-b^2y-cz+d\sinh x\) with \(b,c,d>0\), nontrivial compact invariant dynamics exists exactly when \(a>d\): if \(a\le d\) every bounded forward orbit converges to the origin, every bounded complete orbit is the origin, and the only compactly supported invariant probability measure is \(\delta_0\); if \(a>d\), a unique symmetry pair of nonzero equilibria exists.
limitations: The theorem concerns bounded/compact recurrent dynamics; it does not classify unbounded trajectories when \(a\le d\) or non-equilibrium compact dynamics when \(a>d\).
